trickyParts: The browser's reader counts a blank line toward a list item's spread when no list or quote inside the item is open across it and it is not in the run of line endings the item drops. A directive container is not such a container, so the blank lines that end a typed block are the item's at any depth. Three things keep them from the item: a line the containers around the block do not read as blank; an unclosed fenced code block, which takes them as code; and, in a quote only, a list the block ends with, because resolveContentExits ends that list where the block's content starts on the next line, past the quote's markers. Read off the mdast positions: '- a / C / - x / (blank) / :::' gives list [3:3-3:6], its quoted twin list [3:5-4:2]

The kind 6 exemption had to go rather than be narrowed: a tag of a block-level name opens kind 6 however unfinished, so the exemption cannot tell '<div x' from a whole tag. Kind 7 alone is exempt, which costs the four '</div\t>' documents that did read alike; each has a corpus-errors fixture
